rikai — packet census/mechanism (prioritree-ux): the mechanism map — how the existing FastAPI server fronts the core's five-op interface today. READ-ONLY; no other act performed.

THE CORE'S PUBLIC FACE (src/prioritree/session.py, class Session — the composition layer the wrappers cite):
- register_run(items, operator, quorum=1) → (run_id, RunManifest, count); RegistryRefusedError wrapped into VotesRefusedError.
- next_pair(run_id, seed=None) → the bare (item_a, item_b, count) triple — no state, no scores; fall-through RAISES ExhaustedQueue, the DONE signal (three fields: expected/found/next_action).
- cast_vote(run_id, pair, winner, comparator_id, comparator_class, notes=None, supersedes=None) → the ack quadruple (vote_id, VoteRecord, count, acknowledged).
- read_vote_state(run_id) → VoteCensus (per_pair_counts over the full universe, per_item_counts, the full vote_log) — NEVER refuses on coverage.
- tally_rank(run_id) → frozen TallyResult (ranked_groups, per-item wins/losses/ties, CoverageDatum, algorithm_version); TallyRefusedError = the SAFE HALT — the emission ALWAYS refuses on coverage; write target NOTHING.

THE SERVER'S WIRING (src/prioritree/service.py — the ONLY server module; app = FastAPI() :152, launch uvicorn prioritree.service:app): all five ops exposed REST 1:1, none missing — POST /runs → register (201 {run_id: stem}); GET /runs/{run_id}/next?seed= → serve (200 the pair object; DONE → 200 {done: true + three fields}); POST /runs/{run_id}/votes → cast_vote (200 {vote_id, count, acknowledged}); GET /runs/{run_id}/state → census (200 {total, items}); GET /runs/{run_id}/tally → rank (200 asdict(TallyResult), 409 SAFE HALT). Status map: StoreRefusedError→404 (both families), VotesRefusedError→422, TallyRefusedError→409, ExhaustedQueue→200-DONE, RequestValidationError re-badged→400, uncaught→500 crash envelope. Refusals caught BY TYPE, rendered at one point (render_refusal).

THE STATE MECHANISM (the chain, named): (1) module-level per-process seam — app.state.seam = Serialize(STORE_HOME) at import; STORE_HOME = Path(".prioritree/runs"), CWD-relative (run_store.py:53). (2) per-request reconstruction under ONE process-wide threading.Lock — each Serialize verb acquires once around Persist.load + the act whole (service_store.py:118-208); load pre-pass-validates the JSONL file and rebuilds a FRESH in-memory door (Session(Registry()), re-register, in-order re-casts — run_store.py:684-705), so the dedup index is fresh by construction. (3) lifetime: lock/seam = process; in-memory core = one request; the append-only JSONL run files on disk are the only cross-request state (save-at-cast, one line + flush per write). Multi-process banked under single-worker.

THE SEAMS (envelope vs the core's ruled return forms): (1) register — the (run_id, manifest, count) triple collapses to {run_id: stem} alone, and the wire's id is the FILE STEM, not the core's in-file handle (two id spaces, run_store.py:536-539); (2) cast — VoteRecord ELIDED from the ack (durable in the file only); (3) state — vote_log and per_pair_counts elided ({"total","items"} only; "the stamps re-mint at load — rendering lies"); (4) tally — coverage.pair_counts re-keyed Pair→"item_a|item_b" strings (JSON keys; the one priced reconciliation); (5) DONE — the core's RAISED signal becomes a 200 VALUE body; (6) the 400 re-badge carries FastAPI's native {detail: [...]} grammar, NOT the three-field form; the 500 fabricates a three-part envelope with no core counterpart. Ruled properties holding at the wire: the state read never refuses on coverage; the tally always refuses on it (409); rank appends nothing.

THE LAW (cited): R5, Q-ux-surface ruling 5 (ux store) — every 4xx/5xx body carries expected/found/next-action, never a bare status, never a stack leak, never a silent OK where a refusal belongs; ground, the collaborator verbatim: "the api absolutely does not follow the errors teach methodology. So, we are going to have to fix that as we go." THE SERVER: exactly one — src/prioritree/service.py (the only fastapi import in the tree); five routes; zero HTTPException anywhere in src; two app-level exception handlers (the 400 re-badge; the 500 fold).

THE GAP MAP (21 error paths over 5 endpoints):
- POST /runs — 404 render_refusal (compliant) · 422 render_refusal (compliant) · malformed body => 400 {"detail": [...]} — string-detail · uncaught => 500 three-part fold (compliant).
- GET /runs/{run_id}/next — 404/422 render_refusal (compliant) · DONE => 200 {done: true, expected, found, next_action} — a ruled STATE, honest, not a silent-ok · ?seed=<non-int> => 400 detail family — string-detail · 500 fold (compliant).

THE SEAM: the core's refusal grammar is carried WHOLE. All four typed signals (StoreRefusedError, VotesRefusedError, ExhaustedQueue, TallyRefusedError) construct expected/found/next_action as data attributes; the seam rides them through BY TYPE, never wrapped, never conflated; one render point reads them as data, never str(e) reparsed; no ruled refusal type escapes the catch tables — anything else is a genuine crash into the three-part 500 fold. THE HONEST CONDITION: R5's premise and the tree diverge — the service face already renders ThreePart on every path its own routes catch (404/422/409/500 all carry the three fields; no stack leak; DONE honest at 200). The residue is exactly two families: the 400 re-badge's native detail grammar (fireable on register, serve's seed, cast) and the framework-default 404/405. No bare-status, no default-422, no stack-leak, no silent-ok, no absent path found. The premise matches the residue, not the whole — that is the state.

COUNT: endpoints: 5, error paths: 21 (incl. 2 framework-default surface paths), ThreePart-compliant today: 16 — the 5 gaps all string-detail: ×3 the 400 re-badge family, ×2 the framework-default 404/405.

suisen's completion report (packet design/presentation, prioritree-ux) — the tally presentation recommendation:

THE RECOMMENDATION, WHOLE: one route (GET /runs/{run_id}/tally), one generated screen family with TWO exclusive renderings — the RANKED WHOLE (200, done: true) and the SAFE HALT (409) — branched at the wire's outcome, rendered from a Python view model, Shoelace chrome via CDN, Jinja2 the renderer, zero client-side derivation, one fetch (never a second endpoint summoned to decorate either state). The binary IS the domain's (R12 strictly binary); the presentation mirrors it — never a partial ranking dressed as whole, never a halt dressed as failure.

THE RANKED WHOLE SCREEN: a semantic table, one rowspan'd rank cell per tie group — competition ranking (1, 2, 2, 4; dense lies about position), members in the frozen id-order verbatim (never re-sorted). Per-item stats: W/L/T integers verbatim plus comparisons (W+L+T — the one derivation the frozen contract sanctions); NO win-fraction column — the score is the tally's internal mechanism (R10); the projection law forbids the presentation re-deriving what the tally rules. The coverage line: one muted strip (pairs-at-quorum, "graph connected (1 component)", cycle named) with the full datum in sl-details; the named cycle rendered as a NEUTRAL tag with its directed edges + the R11 one-liner (structural, dissolved into win fractions — data quality, never an error, never danger-red); pair_counts matrix under sl-details, keys re-split on "|" (the wire's re-keyed form). The version stamp: footer badge, algorithm_version VERBATIM ("win-rate-v1") — the auditability contract.

THE SAFE HALT SCREEN: the refusal IS the screen — three labeled regions (Expected / Found / Next-action) rendering the 409 body's fields VERBATIM (R5: the same grammar on wire and screen; the body is the source, never re-computed). Found structured from the domain's own deterministic section grammar: zero-coverage items, components, under-quorum pairs as badges. Next-action = the cure, two kinds never conflated: bridging pairs ("connectivity needs NEW comparisons") vs shortfall pairs ("quorum needs MORE VOTES") — sl-tags grouped by kind. One button: resume the sitting → the compare flow (the scheduler serves exactly the under-quorum pairs; no pair-picker — comparator pair-gaming foreclosed by construction). NO ranking content — not grayed, not collapsed, not "provisional" (R12, absolute).

THE DONE-vs-HALTED DISTINCTION: branch at the wire (200 done:true → the whole; 409 → the halt) — the generator never re-derives the coverage gate's ruling; a render gate mirrors the domain gate (a body with groups but done:false REFUSES to render); distinct chrome: DONE = success badge, HALT = warning never danger (a legal terminal state, an honest refusal, not a crash); two exclusive templates, zero shared rank content, one route.

THE SHOELACE INVENTORY (CDN form): sl-card ×3 (region containers); semantic <table> + generated CSS (Shoelace ships NO table component — the honest pick; the tie group's unit-ness IS the content); sl-badge (success DONE / warning HALT / neutral ranks — the binary made visible); sl-tag (the named cycle, the closing pairs); sl-tooltip (the R11 one-liner); sl-details (the coverage datum, the pair matrix — O(n²) content collapsed). NO progress bar on either terminal screen: terminal states are binary (R12) and the 409 body carries exactly three fields — "how far along" is the mid-run STATE screen's question (the audit view that never refuses on coverage).

THE OPERATOR-vs-COMPARATOR LINE: mid-run the comparator sees the BARE pair only — the tally screen is not linked from the compare surface, no tally content embeds there (the no-anchoring law held at the presentation layer); mid-run the tally view is the OPERATOR's diagnostic (the honest refusal + the named cure); after DONE the comparator MAY see the whole — the compare flow's DONE body links to the tally (the queue exhausted, the sitting over; both comparator classes human|llm inherit the same screen contract; the later MCP tier inherits it too).

- QUERY read_vote_state — pure read; never refuses on coverage.

The segregation lives at the SERVICE SURFACE (verb/path/response/error contract per lane), not the store: one JSONL store + per-request reconstruction serves both lanes; one render point (render_refusal) serves both lanes' refusals.

- THE DONE SIGNAL — query lane (GET /next): 200 {"done": true, + expected/found/next_action} — a VALUE, a state, never an error; the front end swaps to the completion view off it.
- THE SAFE HALT — query lane (GET /tally): 409 {expected, found, next_action} — R12's grammar verbatim ("at quorum" in expected; found names the isolated items/components; next-action names the exact closing pairs).

# design/flows — suisen's completion report — the UX flows (prioritree-ux)

READ-BACK (files read): this ux store's evidence/Q-ux-surface/census-ground-a.md + census-ground-b.md (five routes 1:1 over the five ops; web state EMPTY — this design is the tier's birth; no runs-list op; launch `uvicorn prioritree.service:app`) + census-mechanism-a.md + census-mechanism-b.md (the wire's envelope shapes, the elisions, the ruled properties); this ux store's junro.json (R1 the stack re-anchored, R2 the CQRS agenda, R5 ThreePart mandatory — verbatim); the birth store's junro.json (Q-frontend-stack :508 the projection law; Q-granularity R1/R2/R3; Q-solution-space R4/R5/R9; Q-problem-space R7/R8/R11/R12); the birth store's evidence/Q-solution-space/suisen.md (the no-anchoring ground: "the bare pair is the only valid elicitation context").

THE LANES (R2): COMMANDS — POST /runs (register, the one manifest append), POST /runs/{id}/votes (cast). QUERIES — GET /runs/{id}/next, /state, /tally (the locked read, appends nothing). HTMX rides the existing five routes 1:1; no new verbs, no merged payloads.

FLOW 1 — LANDING + REGISTER. Screen `landing` (route /): the operator's declaration form — operator id, stated question, verdict set (the weak-order triple, tie per declaration, R4), quorum (default 1, policy-as-data, R8), item rows (id + label) — plus the resume field (run_id entry; no runs-list op exists, the stem the only legal address). hx-post="/runs" → COMMAND → 201 → swap to the ack panel: run_id shown (the wire's file stem), the frozen-run warning ("a changed list is a new run"). Refusals (<2 items, duplicate ids → 422 typed three-key) render inline ThreePart (R5); the form pre-checks the common refusals before the wire; the 400 re-badge is not yet ThreePart — the service unit's brief carries the cure (R5 as-we-go). RECOMMEND: one screen, register + resume. Why: one list, one operator, one sitting (Q-granularity R1) — the journey begins at registration; the ruled surface serves both entries.

FLOW 2 — THE SITTING. Screen `sitting` (/runs/{id}): the stated question as prompt; the BARE pair — two cards, labels only, canonical id-sorted order as served (R7); verdict buttons from the DECLARED set; comparator id entry, class human stamped (Q-solution-space R5). NOTHING else — no scores, no counts, no ranking; the envelope's count fields render nowhere here. Steps: pair renders (hx-get next → QUERY) → verdict (hx-post votes → COMMAND) → ack strip (vote_id + acknowledged; the loud idempotent ack names the original handle, R9; count unrendered) → the ack embeds hx-trigger="load" hx-get next into the pair region → next pair. A 422 vote refusal leaves the pair intact — same pair retryable. DONE body → screen `sitting-done`: "every pair judged", the DONE body's expected/found (coverage safe to show — no elicitation remains), link to the ranked whole. No seed control surfaces. RECOMMEND: the two-step chain (POST ack → GET next), never a merged round-trip. Why: the pair NEVER rides a command's response — the no-anchoring boundary architectural, not incidental; a refused vote cannot clobber the pair. RECOMMEND: hide every count from the comparator. Why: the bare pair is the only valid elicitation context; pair-count is ambient information the judgment does not need.

FLOW 3 — PROGRESS. Screen `progress` (a separate route, NEVER embedded in sitting): the census read rendered verbatim — total + per-item involvement ({"total","items"}; per_pair_counts elided at the seam — not resurrected). The comparator MAY see: the pair, the question, the buttons, their own identity and ack. Only the OPERATOR may see: totals, per-item counts, the audit fold. Mid-run ranking cannot leak by navigation — the 409 SAFE HALT refuses until coverage (the honest boundary does the hiding). hx-get state, hx-trigger every 5s → QUERY (never refuses on coverage). RECOMMEND: a separate screen the operator navigates to deliberately. Why: ops 2+4 must not merge — "the comparator surface must not see state; merging leaks the ranking to the judge"; surface separation makes the leak a deliberate act, never ambient.

FLOW 4 — THE RANKED WHOLE. Screen `ranked-whole`: the stated question as heading; the ranked groups in order, ties as shared-rank groups (stable id-order, R12); the audit in a details region (per-item W/L/T, components, the cycle named as data quality never hidden — R11, algorithm_version). SAFE HALT (409) → screen `safe-halt`: the refusal rendered verbatim ThreePart — Expected (scheduled coverage) / Found (isolated items, components) / Next-action (the exact closing pairs) + the cure links (resume, progress). NEVER a partial ranking dressed as whole (R12). hx-get tally → QUERY. RECOMMEND: render the frozen result verbatim — never re-sort, re-group, re-derive. Why: byte-identical re-runs (R12) — the web must not become a second tally; the 409's ThreePart body IS the display text — the web renders refusals, never authors them.

FLOW 5 — THE RESUME. A stopped-anywhere sitting is legal (Q-granularity R1: append-only store + pure tally). The operator returns → landing's resume field (run_id) → sitting → GET /next serves the next under-quorum pair (default seed from run_id; replays byte-match) → comparator identity re-enters (the stamp is per-vote; a resumed sitting may be a different seat) → continues → vote or DONE (the DONE body arrives if the schedule was exhausted). Resume IS the next_pair query — the wire serves manifest + ledger + the skip of covered pairs; QUERY until the first vote (the first COMMAND). RECOMMEND: no resume op, no session token, no client-side sitting state. Why: the ground already made resume representable; web-tier sitting state would mint a second source of truth the no-anchoring law would then police — refused by construction, not diligence.

THE PROJECTION NOTE (R1): every screen is a Jinja2 slot in the generator's source structure — landing, sitting, sitting-done, progress, ranked-whole, safe-halt + the fragments (register-ack, vote-ack, the one refusal renderer) — Shoelace via CDN, Web Components under separation of concerns, ALL rendered from Python; hand-authored artifacts out of grammar. # design/blind-walk — moho's completion report — what breaks when nobody helps

READ-BACK (files read): this ux store's reports/design/flows.md (the walked flows 1–5) + reports/design/presentation.md (the terminal screens) + two blind probes: glob src/prioritree/** (the API tier exists — service.py, five ops) and glob **/*.html (ZERO templates — no live web surface; the walked glass is the design as written).

THE WALK, COLD, PER STEP (screen serves → what I need → where it breaks):
1. LANDING "/": a form serves operator id, stated question, verdict set, quorum, item rows, a resume field. Breaks: nothing says what this site IS or what happens after submit; "operator id" unexplained (chosen? minted? does it matter?); "verdict set — the weak-order triple" is jargon I cannot act on; quorum (default 1) never explained — I can set 2 and quietly doom the run; item-id rules unknown until refused; the RESUME field wants a run_id with no shape, no example, no where-to-find — and no runs-list exists, so a lost token is lost forever.
2. REGISTER ACK: run_id shown + "a changed list is a new run". Breaks: NO link from ack to the sitting is stated anywhere — my only stated path to judging is retyping the token I just received into the resume field; no "save this"/copy affordance named; the warning names a future I cannot reach (no edit op exists); for quorum>1 no share/invite affordance — recruiting the second judge is unaddressed on every screen.
3. THE SITTING: question + two label-only cards + verdict buttons from the declared set + comparator id entry. Breaks: WHY a comparator id — I registered as operator, nobody says these are the same person; the button↔card mapping is UNSPECIFIED — the two docs never tie a button to a card, and cards carry labels only (ids hidden, id-sorted invisible), so if buttons read a/b-flavored I must GUESS which backs which card; a consistent wrong guess silently reverses the whole ranking and no signal ever disconfirms it.
4. VOTE ACK → NEXT: the ack strip (vote_id + acknowledged) auto-loads the next pair. Breaks: the ack never restates WHAT I chose (no "you preferred X over Y") — mis-clicks and mis-mappings are undetectable at the only moment they are checkable; counts hidden by design leaves no horizon (10 pairs? 10,000?); the operator's progress screen exists but no stated link reaches it.
5. 422 MID-SITTING: the pair stays, refusal renders verbatim three-key. Serves OK (pair intact, same-pair retry). Breaks: no pre-check on the comparator id — my first refusal teaches me the field I never understood; the wire's machine grammar renders verbatim by ruling — readable to the seats, alien to me.
6. DONE "every pair judged": Breaks: "judged" means MY queue, not the run's coverage — with quorum>1 my done is the run's not-done; the "ranked whole" link can land me on a 409 I cannot act on ("I did my job — why refused?").
7. RANKED WHOLE + SAFE HALT: the table reads (competition ranks, tie groups, W/L/T). Breaks: "graph connected (1 component)" and the components badges are graph theory with no plain gloss (the cycle earns a one-liner; components earn none); the cycle one-liner cites "win fractions" — a number the table deliberately hides; the halt's "resume the sitting" presumes I know more judges exist — WHO provides the "NEW comparisons"/"MORE VOTES" is never said, and a solo operator's cure is unstated (re-sit under a new comparator id?); the seats disagree on the halt's affordances (flows.md: cure links resume+progress; presentation.md: "one button").
8. RESUME (a day later): token → landing resume field → sitting re-serves. Breaks: depends entirely on a once-shown opaque token being preserved; no "where you left off" — the returning me cannot tell a fresh pair from one already judged, and a quorum-echo pair (idempotent ack) is indistinguishable from new work; the returning user who wants the RESULT funnels through the sitting — no direct result address on the landing.

THE WALK'S VERDICT: the design serves the domain flawlessly (honest refusals, unanchored pairs, legal halts) and the user barely — the wire's grammar is projected into the glass verbatim, and the cold user inherits the engineers' nouns (components, quorum, weak-order, comparator) with no bridge. The three breaks that lose users: the button↔card guess (silent vote corruption), the ack→sitting gap (the fresh registrant's dead end), done-vs-coverage (the completed user refused).

# design/adversarial — hyoka's completion report — the design whole attacked against the rulings and the seams

READ-BACK (files read): reports/design/flows.md + cqrs-mapping.md + presentation.md (whole, the design whole) · the census set whole (.junro/evidence/Q-ux-surface/census-ground-a/b, census-mechanism-a/b, census-error-shape-a/b) · the ux store's junro.json (R1-R6 verbatim) · the birth store's junro.json (Q-granularity R1/R2/R3/R6, Q-solution-space R4/R5/R9/R10, Q-problem-space R7/R8/R11/R12, Q-frontend-stack) · birth evidence/Q-solution-space/suisen.md (the no-anchoring ground) · src/prioritree/service.py (whole — the wire's request/response shapes verified at source, not assumed from the census).

THE VERDICT FIRST: the design does NOT meet the bar as written — three blocking findings, all one family: the screens consume wire surfaces that do not exist. The lanes, the no-anchoring architecture, and the R10-R12 presentation discipline hold; the wire-seams do not.

BLOCKING 1 — THE JSON/HTML CONTRADICTION (flows.md FLOWS 1-4 × cqrs-mapping §2). The flows point HTMX at the five routes and design rendered panels off their responses ("swap to the ack panel: run_id shown…", "the ack embeds hx-get next", "DONE body → screen sitting-done", the 5s state poll); cqrs-mapping §2 rules the same surface "current routes 1:1 — CONFIRMED, no amendment" — and every route returns a JSON body (service.py :253/:283/:319/:346/:393). HTMX swaps the response body into the DOM: a JSON body renders as raw text, and the crude fallback renders the cast ack's `count` and the next body's `count` INTO the comparator's sight — breaching FLOW 2's own "hide every count from the comparator" (the no-anchoring ground: ops 2+4 must not merge). Forced answer: the synthesis NAMES the mechanism — (a) the web tier's own fragment routes (amending §2 to "no op-surface amendment; the web tier's route surface named"), or (b) content negotiation on the five routes (HX-Request → a Jinja2 fragment; JSON preserved for non-HTMX clients, the pinned tests untouched). Unnamed, no buildable web brief exists.

BLOCKING 2 — THE MANIFEST READ GAP (flows.md FLOW 2/4/5). The sitting screen renders "the stated question as prompt" + "verdict buttons from the DECLARED set"; the ranked whole renders "the stated question as heading"; FLOW 5's resume "may be a different seat". No read route serves the manifest: /next = {item_a,item_b,count} (:283), /state = {total,items} (:346), /tally = asdict(TallyResult) — no question, no verdict set (:393); register's 201 elides it (census-mechanism-b seam 1). The elicitation context itself — R3's operator binding made visible — is unservable, and the ruled layering (the web fronts the service, Q-setup-arch) forbids the web tier reading the store. Forced answer: rule the manifest-read mechanism into the SERVICE unit's brief (a sixth query at core + wire — manifest lookups already ruled deterministic at Q-solution-space — or an amended read response) BEFORE it lands; cqrs-mapping's "no amendment" locks the very surface the web unit depends on.

BLOCKING 3 — THE VERDICT-SET FIELD HAS NO WIRE HOME (flows.md FLOW 1 × R4). The register form carries "verdict set (the weak-order triple, tie per declaration, R4)" — RegisterRunRequest accepts items/operator_id/question/quorum ONLY (service.py :113-116); the route stamps the default triple (:246). R4's "tie per the operator's declaration" is undeclarable over the wire: the field silently drops (the operator believes a declaration landed — a silent lie, against R5's own spirit) or the wire is amended. Forced answer: drop the field and render the ruled default honestly, or amend the request model — ruled in the brief, never discovered mid-build.

MEDIUM 4 — THE ERROR-SWAP MECHANISM UNDESIGNED (cqrs-mapping §2's own deferral). The flows depend on non-2xx swaps as load-bearing — FLOW 1's inline 422 refusals, FLOW 2's retryable pair, FLOW 4's whole safe-halt screen off the 409 body — yet "HTMX swaps nothing on non-2xx by default" is deferred unnamed: the mechanism class (response-targets extension = a client dep; 200-wrapping = R5's silent-OK breach; page navigation) must be named. Also unaddressed: FLOW 5's unknown-run resume (the first GET /next 404s into the pair region, no designed rendering), the web tier's own 500-fold rendering, and the new page routes' 404/405. The census's 5 gap-cures are mapped and ride the right brief — those hold.

MEDIUM 5 — THE GENERATOR ASSERTED, NOT DESIGNED (R1 + G-UX-DESIGN-BRIEF's "the projection architecture"). The reports name screens as "Jinja2 slots" and the Shoelace inventory but never design the generator: its source structure, its emission + regen/check channel (the scaffold's own --check idiom), what lands vs what is gitignored. Hand-authoring sneaks in at exactly this seam: FLOW 1's "the form pre-checks the common refusals before the wire" is client-side logic — authored JS breaches R1 — and it duplicates the registry's refusal rules (a second source of truth under content-in-configuration). Also unnamed: HTMX's own delivery (Shoelace is ruled via CDN; the wire library is not) and the jinja2 dependency (census-ground-b §6: absent from pyproject).

MEDIUM-LOW 6 — THE NO-ANCHORING RESIDUE, PRICED BUT UNRULED. The law holds architecturally (bare pair, counts unrendered, the pair never rides a command's response, the 409 does the hiding, no seed control). The residue: /state and /tally are unauthenticated and URL-reachable — a comparator CAN deliberately self-anchor (per-item exposure ambient on the progress screen). flows.md prices it ("a deliberate act, never ambient") — defensible, but the brief must carry the acceptance explicitly for the collaborator's ruling, not inherit it silently.

LOW 7 — THE ORDERING FRAME. The service unit lands FIRST with its surface locked "no amendment" — Blockers 1-3's reconciliations must ride ITS brief or the web unit breaks mid-build. The lifecycle unit's constraints (port/host policy — "Port: NOT stated in src", census-ground-a; single-worker launch) are never handed forward; the brief should carry them.

THE HELD LINES (the met half, cited for fairness): the CQRS lanes clean — 2 commands / 3 queries, no conflation (the ack-embeds-get is a trigger chain, never a merge); the elisions respected (per_pair_counts not resurrected, VoteRecord unrendered, pair_counts re-split on "|"); the two id spaces ruled stem-only; R10 held (no win-fraction column — the score never re-derived); R11 held (the cycle neutral, data quality); R12 held (binary terminals, never partial dressed as whole, the 409 rendered verbatim — the web renders refusals, never authors them); R6 held (the reports seat-authored).

THE CALL: BLOCKED at the design bar — the three wire-seam blockers must be reconciled and ruled in togo's synthesis before G-UX-DESIGN-BRIEF can honestly green; the mediums ride the brief as named mechanisms, never deferred holes.

# THE DESIGN BRIEF — the reconciled UX whole (prioritree-ux, synthesize/ux-design, togo)

READ-BACK (files read, the whole ground): the design lane's five seat-authored reports — reports/design/flows.md, cqrs-mapping.md, presentation.md, adversarial.md (hyoka's BLOCK), blind-walk.md (moho's breaks) · the census evidence whole — .junro/evidence/Q-ux-surface/census-ground-a.md + census-ground-b.md, census-mechanism-a.md + census-mechanism-b.md, census-error-shape-a.md + census-error-shape-b.md · the ux store's junro.json (Q-ux-surface R1–R6 verbatim) · the birth store's junro.json (Q-granularity R1/R2/R3; Q-solution-space R4/R5/R9/R10 + THE SPLIT + the five-op interface; Q-problem-space R7/R8/R11/R12; Q-frontend-stack; Q-setup-arch) · the wire at source: src/prioritree/service.py (whole), session.py (whole), registry.py (whole), service_store.py (whole), run_store.py (the Persist class: register/load/the manifest line) · this store's packets.jsonl (my dispatch). READ-ONLY held — nothing written beyond this report.

## §0 THE RECONCILIATION VERDICT

Hyoka's three blockers are ONE family — the screens consume wire surfaces that do not exist — and all three are answered here with NAMED mechanisms, each an amendment-pending-ruling for the collaborator at G-UX-DESIGN-BRIEF: (1) the web tier owns its own fragment/page route set (the JSON routes stay pure); (2) a sixth query serves the manifest; (3) the verdict-set field is dropped, source-ruled. The mediums are designed, not deferred: the error-swap mechanism (rendering routes), the generator (source structure → artifacts, --check-guarded), the no-anchoring acceptance (explicit, carried to the gate). Moho's breaks are folded into the flows as named affordances. The held lines stay held (hyoka's own list, §14). THE BRIEF IS THE SPEC — exact, buildable, nothing left to interpret.

## §1 BLOCKER 1 — THE JSON/HTML MECHANISM: WEB-TIER FRAGMENT ROUTES (the ruling)

THE CONTRADICTION (adversarial.md Blocking 1): the flows point HTMX at the five JSON routes; cqrs-mapping §2 confirms the same surface "no amendment"; HTMX swaps the JSON body into the DOM — raw text, and the crude fallback renders the `count` fields INTO the comparator's sight, breaching FLOW 2's own hide-every-count law.

THE MECHANISM, NAMED: the web tier owns its own route set — PAGE routes (full documents) and FRAGMENT routes (swap targets) — generated per R1. HTMX points at the fragment routes, NEVER at the JSON routes. The fragment/page controllers are true HTTP clients of the service surface over the SAME app in-process (the ASGI-transport client pattern — no socket, no port, no second process; the exact client pinned at the web unit's brief). Q-setup-arch's layering held literally: the web fronts the SERVICE (the five+six JSON routes), never the seam, never the store — hyoka's own blocker-2 clause.

THE REASONING (why fragment routes, not HX-Request content negotiation on the five routes):
1. THE ORDERING LAW (hyoka's Low 7): the service unit lands FIRST with its surface locked. Fragment routes keep the service surface FINAL at its landing — the five routes JSON-only forever, the web unit never re-opens them. Content negotiation forces one of two broken horns: the inversion (the service unit landing render branches that need the web tier's generated templates — the dependency pointing backwards), or the mid-build amendment (the web unit re-opening five landed routes). The pipeline law refuses both.
2. THE TIER SEPARATION (R1 + Q-setup-arch): service.py stays the machine surface — the JSON wire the pinned tests assert byte-exact, the surface the later MCP tier inherits pure (the composition's own banked note). The HTML lives in the web tier's generated module, its own grammar, its own generator.
3. THE CQRS LANES HOLD EITHER WAY (R2, the dispatch's own condition) — and ride CLEANER here: the web tier's backend communication IS the service surface; the fragment routes issue the service's commands on POST and queries on GET, the lanes the mapping ruled (§9).
4. THE NO-ANCHORING GUARANTEE STRENGTHENS: the fragment controllers construct the render contexts — the `count` fields never enter any sitting-context template context (dropped at the controller; kensho's verification pins it). Under negotiation the count rides every response into the swap boundary — the leak hyoka priced.

THE CONSEQUENCE FOR THE SERVICE UNIT'S BRIEF (named): NO HTML at the service tier — no templates, no HX-Request branch, no Jinja2 in service.py, ever. Its brief carries: the five routes' shapes FROZEN as landed (the pinned tests untouched) + the sixth query (§2) + the ThreePart cures (§10) + nothing else touching its routes. The ONE service.py touch the web unit makes: the mount line at the module's tail (the web tier's route registration, one line — named in §12, carried by the WEB unit's brief, landed after the web routes exist).

## §2 BLOCKER 2 — THE SIXTH QUERY (the manifest read, named: verb + path + response form)

THE GAP (adversarial.md Blocking 2): no read route serves the manifest — /next = {item_a, item_b, count} (ids, not labels — session.py:222 schedules over ids), /state = {total, items}, /tally = the frozen result, register's 201 elides it. The sitting screen's WHOLE elicitation context — R3's operator binding made visible (the stated question, the declared verdict set, the id→label map, the quorum) — is unservable, and the layering forbids the web tier reading the store. THE AMENDMENT: cqrs-mapping §2's "current routes 1:1 — CONFIRMED, no amendment" is AMENDED BY THIS RECONCILIATION — the service surface grows ONE query route; the five routes' own shapes stand untouched.

THE SIXTH QUERY:
- VERB: GET — the query lane, a locked read, appends nothing (R2's segregation; the write-target-NOTHING law inherited).
- PATH: /runs/{run_id}/manifest — REST-parallel to /state and /tally; {run_id} is the FILE STEM, the wire's id law held (cqrs-mapping §5).
- RESPONSE 200: {"run_id": <the stem echoed>, "question": <the stated question>, "verdicts": <the declared set as a sorted array>, "quorum": <the declared policy-as-data>, "items": [[id, label], ...] — payload order preserved}. # The framework-refusal statuses (named per the zero-magic-value-in-src
```python
# discipline — the handler branches on them; the codes FROZEN: the cure flips
# BODIES only, never the machine-dispatchable statuses).
_NOT_FOUND: Final[int] = 404
_METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED: Final[int] = 405


@app.exception_handler(StarletteHTTPException)
def refuse(request: Request, exc: StarletteHTTPException) -> JSONResponse:
    """Refuse the framework's bare HTTP exceptions in the family grammar — 404/405 taught.

    Purpose: R5's census cure ×2 — the framework's routing refusals ride bare
    from Starlette ({"detail": "Not Found"} / {"detail": "Method Not
    Allowed"}); this handler renders them in the family grammar CONSTRUCTED
    from the request's own address — expected the method + path as addressed
    (the fold's own _attempted form), found the routing violation named (404:
    no route matches the path; 405: the method not allowed at the path), and
    next_action the route table's legal lanes (the route/method set taught —
    the constant cited, content-in-configuration). The STATUS rides
    exc.status_code verbatim — the codes FROZEN (machine-dispatchable; the
    acceptance harness's 404-as-ready probe rides the status, untouched);
    any other StarletteHTTPException (none raised by this surface) carries
    the family fields with found the framework's own detail. The typed
    refusals ride through BY TYPE untouched — the routes' catch tables stand;
    this handler never sees them.
    Refuses when: never — the handler renders; the framework's refusal IS the
    input (exc.status_code + exc.detail, never re-derived).
    Re-run: deterministic — the same request renders the same body.
    Touches: nothing — a rendering over the exception and the request's own
    method and path.
    Provenance: the service unit brief §3 (cure 2 — the framework defaults),
    the ux design §10 (the cure map), R5, G-SERVICE-FACE.
    """
    _address = f"{request.method} {request.url.path}"
    if exc.status_code == _NOT_FOUND:
        _found = f"no route matches the path {request.url.path}"
    elif exc.status_code == _METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED:
        _found = f"the method {request.method} is not allowed at the path {request.url.path}"
    else:
        _found = exc.detail
    return JSONResponse(
        status_code=exc.status_code,
        content={EXPECTED: _address, FOUND: _found, NEXT_ACTION: _ROUTE_TABLE},
    )
```

```python
# Copyright (C) 2026 Mark Losey. All rights reserved.
"""web — the web fronts: the child app over the service's wire, the nine routes.

The web unit (web-brief §1.1 + the approved design §8): the CHILD application
(FastAPI with the docs routes disabled — the web tier is the human's surface,
not an API), mounted at the service app's TAIL (service.py's mount line, the
one touch); the nine routes (5 pages at honest statuses + 4 rendering
fragments at 200); the in-process service client (httpx2.AsyncClient over
ASGITransport against the imported service app — raise_app_exceptions=False
REQUIRED: the service fold sends its envelope then always re-raises, and the
fold case needs the envelope RETURNED, rikai finding 1 ruled); the child's OWN
fold + refuse handlers (the mount's price: after the tail mount every path
the parent does not fully match lands on the child — starlette routing.py
serves the FIRST FULL match and the Mount matches FULL on path alone, so the
child owns the unmatched-path and disallowed-method surface; its refuse
handler renders the IDENTICAL family grammar as a JSONResponse so the pinned
parent-face arcs survive unedited); the no-anchoring law held by
construction (the count fields are UNREAD at every sitting-context controller
— they never enter a render context); the fragment routes parse form bodies
MANUALLY (no typed Form fields: FastAPI's validation 422 would emit outside
the family grammar, and the fragment tier holds no 4xx — the wire is the sole
validator). All imports via fastapi/starlette's re-export surface + httpx2
(the lock's name — NEVER `import httpx`, the stale unlocked venv copy;
alias_httpx() library-forbidden). Five-field docstrings on every public
symbol; content-in-configuration (the paths and template names named
constants); no asserts, no prints.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any, Final

from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse, RedirectResponse, Response
from fastapi.staticfiles import StaticFiles
from fastapi.templating import Jinja2Templates
from starlette.exceptions import HTTPException as StarletteHTTPException

import httpx2

from prioritree.service import ESCALATION, app as service_app
from prioritree.web_structure import UNION_LANES

__all__ = ["web_app"]

# The web tier's named constants (content-in-configuration): the route paths
# (the child's own surface, collision-free against the service's six), the
# emission homes (CWD-relative, the repo-root launch discipline), the
# in-process client's base URL (httpx demands absolute URLs — a literal the
# transport ignores: no socket, no port, no second process).
_LANDING: Final[str] = "/"
_SITTING: Final[str] = "/runs/{stem}"
_DONE: Final[str] = "/runs/{stem}/done"
_PROGRESS: Final[str] = "/runs/{stem}/progress"
_RESULT: Final[str] = "/runs/{stem}/result"
_REGISTER: Final[str] = "/ui/register"
_PAIR: Final[str] = "/ui/runs/{stem}/pair"
_VOTE: Final[str] = "/ui/runs/{stem}/vote"
_STATE_STRIP: Final[str] = "/ui/runs/{stem}/state"
_TEMPLATES_HOME: Final[str] = "web/templates"
_STATIC_HOME: Final[str] = "web/static"
_BASE_URL: Final[str] = "http://prioritree.internal"
_OK: Final[int] = 200
_CREATED: Final[int] = 201
_NOT_FOUND: Final[int] = 404
_METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED: Final[int] = 405
_UNPROCESSABLE: Final[int] = 422
_CONFLICT: Final[int] = 409
_CRASH: Final[int] = 500
_SEE_OTHER: Final[int] = 303
_FRAGMENT_LANE: Final[str] = "/ui/"

# The child app (web-brief §3e: the docs routes DISABLED — the parent's own
# /docs, /redoc, /openapi.json stay live, registered before the mount).
web_app = FastAPI(docs_url=None, redoc_url=None, openapi_url=None)
web_app.mount("/static", StaticFiles(directory=_STATIC_HOME), name="static")
templates = Jinja2Templates(directory=_TEMPLATES_HOME)

# THE IN-PROCESS CLIENT (web-brief §3a, ruled exact): ONE module-level
# instance, built at import against the imported service app, shared by all
# controllers, process-lifetime — no per-request construction, no teardown
# (ASGITransport holds no socket). raise_app_exceptions=False REQUIRED.
_client = httpx2.AsyncClient(
    base_url=_BASE_URL,
    transport=httpx2.ASGITransport(app=service_app, raise_app_exceptions=False),
)


async def _service(method: str, path: str, json: Any | None = None) -> httpx2.Response:
    """Call the service over the in-process client — the one service path.

    Purpose: every controller's service lane rides this one call (the layering
    held mechanically: the web tier is a true HTTP client of the service
    surface over the same app — its stack, its fold, its door).
    Refuses when: never — the response (any status) IS the return.
    Re-run: deterministic given the store state.
    Touches: nothing — the transport is in-process.
    Provenance: web-brief §3a (the async form), rikai finding 1, G-WEB.
    """
    return await _client.request(method, path, json=json)


def _labels(manifest: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Map the manifest's items to labels — the id->label law (design §7a).

    Purpose: build {id: label} from the manifest body's [[id, label], ...]
    rows — the sitting cards and the ranked whole render labels, ids the
    stable key; an id absent from the map falls back to the id itself.
    Refuses when: never — a pure projection over the manifest's own rows.
    Re-run: deterministic.
    Touches: nothing.
    Provenance: the design §2 (the sixth query's response form), §7a, G-WEB.
    """
    return {str(row[0]): str(row[1]) for row in manifest["items"]}


def _fields(body: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Read a ThreePart body's three fields as data — the one read point.

    Purpose: the service wire's every refusal (and the DONE state's own
    three fields) carries expected/found/next_action; this one function
    reads them as data for the render contexts — never re-derived (the body
    is the source, the web renders, never authors).
    Refuses when: never — a pure read over the body's own keys.
    Re-run: deterministic.
    Touches: nothing.
    Provenance: R5 (the ThreePart mandate), web-brief §5, G-WEB.
    """
    return {
        "expected": str(body["expected"]),
        "found": str(body["found"]),
        "next_action": str(body["next_action"]),
    }


def _unknown(request: Request, body: dict[str, Any]) -> Response:
    """Render the unknown-run page at the honest 404.

    Purpose: every page route's unknown-stem branch — the landing's resume
    affordance + the wire's own found field (the live set, verbatim).
    Refuses when: never — the 404 IS the input; the page renders honestly.
    Re-run: deterministic.
    Touches: nothing.
    Provenance: web-brief §5 (the 404 page), the design §4, G-WEB.
    """
    return templates.TemplateResponse(
        request, "unknown.html", {"fields": _fields(body)}, status_code=_NOT_FOUND
    )


def _refuse_fragment(request: Request, fields: dict[str, str], fold: bool = False) -> Response:
    """Render the ONE refusal renderer as a fragment at 200.

    Purpose: the fragment inventory's refusal member (never its own route):
    the three fields labeled verbatim + the cure affordance beside them, at
    200 — core HTMX swaps it; the refusal is SEEN, never a silent OK. The
    fold flag renders the crash envelope's escalation wording (§5's fold
    case: the fragment controller receiving 500, or itself raising — the
    same renderer, the envelope's three fields).
    Refuses when: never — the refusal IS the input; the fragment renders.
    Re-run: deterministic.
    Touches: nothing.
    Provenance: web-brief §5 (the 422/400 inline refusal + the fold
    fragment), the design §4, R5, G-WEB.
    """
    return templates.TemplateResponse(
        request, "refuse.html", {"fields": fields, "fold": fold}, status_code=_OK
    )


@web_app.exception_handler(StarletteHTTPException)
def refuse(request: Request, exc: StarletteHTTPException) -> JSONResponse:
    """Refuse the child's framework HTTP exceptions in the family grammar — 404/405 taught.

    Purpose: the mount's price, ruled (web-brief §3e): the child owns every
    path the parent does not fully match — this handler renders the
    IDENTICAL family grammar as the parent's shadowed handler, as a
    JSONResponse (the pinned parent-face arcs assert the JSON body):
    expected the method + path as addressed, found the routing violation
    named (404: no route matches the path; 405: the method not allowed at
    the path), next_action the MOUNTED WHOLE's legal set (the nine web
    routes + the six service routes, from the structure's UNION_LANES —
    the mounted whole IS the tree's HTTP face). The status rides
    exc.status_code verbatim — machine-dispatchable.
    Refuses when: never — the handler renders; the framework's refusal IS
    the input (exc.status_code + exc.detail, never re-derived).
    Re-run: deterministic — the same request renders the same body.
    Touches: nothing.
    Provenance: web-brief §3e (the child's own handler), R5, G-WEBSPEC-BRIEF.
    """
    _address = f"{request.method} {request.url.path}"
    if exc.status_code == _NOT_FOUND:
        _found = f"no route matches the path {request.url.path}"
    elif exc.status_code == _METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED:
        _found = f"the method {request.method} is not allowed at the path {request.url.path}"
    else:
        _found = str(exc.detail)
    return JSONResponse(
        status_code=exc.status_code,
        content={"expected": _address, "found": _found, "next_action": UNION_LANES},
    )


@web_app.exception_handler(Exception)
def fold(request: Request, exc: Exception) -> Response:
    """Fold the child's own escapes — the web app's last resort, in the family grammar.

    Purpose: the child is a SEPARATE application (own middleware stack; the
    parent's fold never re-sends once the child's response started) — this
    handler is the child's own catch-all: expected the attempted act, found
    the exception's type + message verbatim, next_action the service fold's
    own ESCALATION constant. FRAGMENT lane (/ui/*): the fold fragment at
    200 (the sitting context preserved — the fold is SEEN, never a stale
    screen). PAGE lane: the honest 500 page. BLE001 rides the named
    pyproject ruling (the service.py precedent re-carried at the child).
    Refuses when: never — the crash IS the input; the handler renders,
    never re-raises.
    Re-run: deterministic in form.
    Touches: nothing.
    Provenance: web-brief §3b (the child's own fold), Q-error-teaching,
    G-WEBSPEC-BRIEF.
    """
    _fields_fold = {
        "expected": f"{request.method} {request.url.path}",
        "found": f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}",
        "next_action": ESCALATION,
    }
    if request.url.path.startswith(_FRAGMENT_LANE):
        return _refuse_fragment(request, _fields_fold, fold=True)
    return templates.TemplateResponse(
        request, "fold.html", {"fields": _fields_fold}, status_code=_CRASH
    )


@web_app.get(_LANDING)
async def landing(request: Request) -> Response:
    """Land the operator — the register form + the plain-words bridges, no service calls.

    Purpose: the static landing: the register form (operator id, stated
    question, quorum, six item rows, the resume field, the direct-result
    field), the site's explanation, the vocabulary statement, the jargon
    bridges — every copy string from the structure (content-in-configuration:
    the copy lives in data, the template renders). The form hx-posts to the
    register fragment; the resume + result fields navigate via the generated
    pt-go component (the Web Components surface, generated from structure).
    Refuses when: never — a static render.
    Re-run: deterministic.
    Touches: nothing — no service call (the only call-free route).
    Provenance: web-brief §4 route 1, the design §7/§8, G-WEBSPEC-BRIEF.
    """
    return templates.TemplateResponse(request, "landing.html", {})


@web_app.get(_SITTING)
async def sitting(request: Request, stem: str) -> Response:
    """Sit the comparator — the question as prompt, the first pair server-side.

    Purpose: consume the manifest (the question, the declared verdicts, the
    quorum) + next (the FIRST PAIR rendered server-side — a pure query
    render; the two-step law bars the POST's RESPONSE from carrying the
    pair, never the page's query). Cards A/B marked + labeled (the label
    map); the count UNREAD — never in the render context (the no-anchoring
    law, by construction). DONE => redirect to the done page; 404 => the
    unknown-run page at the honest 404. The buttons hx-post the vote; the
    comparator entry rides every post.
    Refuses when: never by this hand — the branches render honestly.
    Re-run: deterministic given the store state.
    Touches: nothing — queries only.
    Provenance: web-brief §4 route 2, the design §7a/§8, G-WEBSPEC-BRIEF.
    """
    manifest = await _service("GET", f"/runs/{stem}/manifest")
    if manifest.status_code == _NOT_FOUND:
        return _unknown(request, manifest.json())
    nxt = await _service("GET", f"/runs/{stem}/next")
    if nxt.status_code == _NOT_FOUND:
        return _unknown(request, nxt.json())
    if nxt.status_code == _UNPROCESSABLE:
        return _refuse_fragment(request, _fields(nxt.json()))
    body = nxt.json()
    if body.get("done"):
        return RedirectResponse(f"/runs/{stem}/done", status_code=_SEE_OTHER)
    manifest_body = manifest.json()
    labels = _labels(manifest_body)
    return templates.TemplateResponse(
        request,
        "sitting.html",
        {
            "stem": stem,
            "question": str(manifest_body["question"]),
            "verdicts": list(manifest_body["verdicts"]),
            "quorum": int(manifest_body["quorum"]),
            "item_a": str(body["item_a"]),
            "item_b": str(body["item_b"]),
            "label_a": labels.get(str(body["item_a"]), str(body["item_a"])),
            "label_b": labels.get(str(body["item_b"]), str(body["item_b"])),
        },
    )


@web_app.get(_DONE)
async def done(request: Request, stem: str) -> Response:
    """State the run's coverage honestly — the DONE body's expected verbatim.

    Purpose: consume next (the DONE body — a VALUE, never an error):
    done:true => the coverage statement (the body's expected field VERBATIM —
    "all {N} scheduled pairs at quorum k={K}" — + the plain-words restatement
    + the result link); a pair body (the re-opened edge — the signal is a
    state read, not a latch) => redirect to the sitting page; 404 => the
    unknown-run page.
    Refuses when: never by this hand.
    Re-run: deterministic given the store state.
    Touches: nothing — a query.
    Provenance: web-brief §4 route 3, the design §7c, G-WEBSPEC-BRIEF.
    """
    nxt = await _service("GET", f"/runs/{stem}/next")
    if nxt.status_code == _NOT_FOUND:
        return _unknown(request, nxt.json())
    body = nxt.json()
    if not body.get("done"):
        return RedirectResponse(f"/runs/{stem}", status_code=_SEE_OTHER)
    return templates.TemplateResponse(
        request, "done.html", {"stem": stem, "fields": _fields(body)}, status_code=_OK
    )


@web_app.get(_PROGRESS)
async def progress(request: Request, stem: str) -> Response:
    """Show the operator the census — the state read verbatim, the 5s poll armed.

    Purpose: the OPERATOR's deliberate navigation (never linked from the
    sitting surface): consume state ({"total", "items"} — per_pair_counts
    stays elided at the seam, never resurrected), render the census
    verbatim; the state-strip region carries hx-get to the state fragment
    with the every-5s trigger. 404 => the unknown-run page.
    Refuses when: never by this hand.
    Re-run: deterministic given the store state.
    Touches: nothing — a query.
    Provenance: web-brief §4 route 4, the design §8, G-WEBSPEC-BRIEF.
    """
    result = await _service("GET", f"/runs/{stem}/state")
    if result.status_code == _NOT_FOUND:
        return _unknown(request, result.json())
    body = result.json()
    return templates.TemplateResponse(
        request,
        "progress.html",
        {"stem": stem, "total": int(body["total"]), "items": dict[str, int](body["items"])},
    )


@web_app.get(_RESULT)
async def result(request: Request, stem: str) -> Response:
    """Render the ranked whole, or the safe halt at the honest 409 — the binary held.

    Purpose: consume tally + manifest. 200 => THE RANKED WHOLE (the render
    gate: a body with groups but done:false REFUSES to render — the gated
    branch renders halt.html's no-ranking-content body with the honest
    withholding + the sitting/progress affordances): the semantic table,
    competition ranks (1, 2, 2, 4), tie groups rowspan'd, members in frozen
    id-order, LABELS via the map, W/L/T verbatim + comparisons (the one
    sanctioned derivation), NO win-fraction column, the coverage strip, the
    cycle neutral + the honest-numbers one-liner, pair_counts re-split on
    "|", the algorithm_version footer badge. 409 => the SAFE HALT at the
    HONEST 409, the body's three fields verbatim + the affordances. 404 =>
    the unknown-run page.
    Refuses when: never by this hand — the branches render honestly; the
    ranked whole NEVER renders at done:false (R12, absolute).
    Re-run: deterministic given the store state.
    Touches: nothing — queries.
    Provenance: web-brief §4 route 5, presentation.md (the ruled render),
    R10/R11/R12, G-WEBSPEC-BRIEF.
    """
    tally = await _service("GET", f"/runs/{stem}/tally")
    if tally.status_code == _CONFLICT:
        return templates.TemplateResponse(
            request,
            "halt.html",
            {"stem": stem, "fields": _fields(tally.json()), "gated": False},
            status_code=_CONFLICT,
        )
    if tally.status_code == _NOT_FOUND:
        return _unknown(request, tally.json())
    whole = tally.json()
    if not bool(whole["coverage"]["done"]):
        return templates.TemplateResponse(
            request, "halt.html", {"stem": stem, "gated": True}, status_code=_OK
        )
    labels = _labels((await _service("GET", f"/runs/{stem}/manifest")).json())
    ranked: list[tuple[int, list[str]]] = []
    for group in whole["ranked_groups"]:
        _previous = len(ranked[-1][1]) if ranked else 0
        ranked.append((ranked[-1][0] + _previous if ranked else 1, [str(item) for item in group]))
    ordered = sorted(str(item) for item in whole["per_item_wins"])
    rows = [
        {
            "id": item,
            "label": labels.get(item, item),
            "wins": int(whole["per_item_wins"][item]),
            "losses": int(whole["per_item_losses"][item]),
            "ties": int(whole["per_item_ties"][item]),
        }
        for item in ordered
    ]
    return templates.TemplateResponse(
        request,
        "result.html",
        {
            "stem": stem,
            "ranked": ranked,
            "rows": rows,
            "components": [list(component) for component in whole["coverage"]["components"]],
            "cycle": [list(edge) for edge in whole["coverage"]["cycle"]],
            "pair_counts": dict[str, int](whole["coverage"]["pair_counts"]),
            "algorithm_version": str(whole["algorithm_version"]),
        },
    )


@web_app.post(_REGISTER)
async def register(request: Request) -> Response:
    """Register the run through the form — the ack panel, or the inline refusal at 200.

    Purpose: parse the form MANUALLY (await request.form() — no typed fields:
    the wire is the sole validator), pair the item rows, cast the quorum (a
    non-numeric quorum renders the family grammar inline — constructed at
    the controller, the only web-authored refusal), POST /runs. 201 => the
    register-ack: the BEGIN THE SITTING link, the run_id with the
    click-to-copy affordance (the generated pt-copy component), the
    shareable sitting URL rendered from the REQUEST's own base URL + the
    run path — never a configured port (the port policy lives in the
    lifecycle targets, never in src), shown always, emphasized when
    quorum>1 (the quorum from the form's OWN posted body — the 201 body is
    {"run_id"} alone, no extra call), the frozen-run warning in plain
    words. 422/400 => the ONE refusal renderer inline at 200, at the form.
    Refuses when: never by this hand — the branches render honestly.
    Re-run: deterministic given the store state.
    Touches: the run file through the service (the command).
    Provenance: web-brief §4 route 6, the design §7b, G-WEBSPEC-BRIEF.
    """
    form = await request.form()
    form_ids = [str(value) for value in form.getlist("item-id")]
    form_labels = [str(value) for value in form.getlist("item-label")]
    rows = [
        [item_id, label]
        for item_id, label in zip(form_ids, form_labels, strict=False)
        if item_id.strip() and label.strip()
    ]
    try:
        quorum = int(str(form.get("quorum", "1")))
    except ValueError:
        return _refuse_fragment(
            request,
            {
                "expected": "the quorum field a whole number 1 or greater",
                "found": f"the quorum field carried {form.get('quorum')!r}",
                "next_action": "enter a whole number for the quorum (1 means just you) and re-send",
            },
        )
    payload = {
        "items": rows,
        "operator_id": str(form.get("operator_id", "")),
        "question": str(form.get("question", "")),
        "quorum": quorum,
    }
    outcome = await _service("POST", "/runs", json=payload)
    if outcome.status_code == _CREATED:

@web_app.get(_PAIR)
async def pair(request: Request, stem: str) -> Response:
    """Serve the bare pair as a fragment — or the HX-Redirect on DONE.

    Purpose: consume next (+ the manifest's label map, §7a's label law —
    /next the route's defining call, the map its label-bearing companion).
    200 => the bare-pair fragment (cards A/B marked + labeled; the count
    UNREAD — dropped at the controller); its buttons hx-post the vote as
    the sitting's pair. DONE => the HX-Redirect RESPONSE HEADER to the done
    page (core HTMX's navigation verb — no extension, no JS). 404/422 =>
    the refusal fragment at 200.
    Refuses when: never by this hand.
    Re-run: deterministic given the store state.
    Touches: nothing — a query.
    Provenance: web-brief §4 route 7, the design §7a/§8, G-WEBSPEC-BRIEF.
    """
    nxt = await _service("GET", f"/runs/{stem}/next")
    if nxt.status_code == _NOT_FOUND or nxt.status_code == _UNPROCESSABLE:
        return _refuse_fragment(request, _fields(nxt.json()))
    body = nxt.json()
    if body.get("done"):
        return Response(status_code=_OK, headers={"HX-Redirect": f"/runs/{stem}/done"})
    labels = _labels((await _service("GET", f"/runs/{stem}/manifest")).json())

        request,
        "pair.html",
        {
            "stem": stem,
            "item_a": str(body["item_a"]),
            "item_b": str(body["item_b"]),

            "label_b": labels.get(str(body["item_b"]), str(body["item_b"])),
        },

@web_app.post(_VOTE)
async def vote(request: Request, stem: str) -> Response:
    """Cast the vote through the form — the ack chains to the next pair.

    Purpose: parse the form MANUALLY, POST the service's cast command, then
    the TWO-STEP CHAIN on 200: the vote-ack restates the verdict in
    ITEM-LABEL TERMS (§7a — "you preferred {label_a} (A) over {label_b}
    (B)" / the tie form; acknowledged:false => the idempotent echo in
    words; the count UNREAD, never rendered) and embeds hx-trigger="load" +
    hx-get to the pair fragment targeting the pair region — the POST's
    response NEVER carries the pair; the load fires the fetch. 422/400 =>
    the inline refusal at 200 — THE PAIR REGION UNTOUCHED (the same pair
    retryable: the refusal swaps into the ack region, never the pair
    region). 404/500 => the same renderer with the wire's fields.
    Refuses when: never by this hand — the branches render honestly.
    Re-run: deterministic given the store state.
    Touches: the run file through the service (the command).
    Provenance: web-brief §4 route 8, the design §7a/§8, G-WEBSPEC-BRIEF.
    """
    form = await request.form()
    payload = {
        "pair": [str(form.get("item_a", "")), str(form.get("item_b", ""))],
        "winner": str(form.get("winner", "")),
        "comparator_id": str(form.get("comparator_id", "")),
        "comparator_class": str(form.get("comparator_class", "human")),
    }
    outcome = await _service("POST", f"/runs/{stem}/votes", json=payload)
    if outcome.status_code != _OK:
        return _refuse_fragment(request, _fields(outcome.json()))
    labels = _labels((await _service("GET", f"/runs/{stem}/manifest")).json())
    return templates.TemplateResponse(
        request,
        "vote-ack.html",
        {
            "stem": stem,
            "winner": payload["winner"],
            "acknowledged": bool(outcome.json()["acknowledged"]),
            "label_a": labels.get(payload["pair"][0], payload["pair"][0]),
            "label_b": labels.get(payload["pair"][1], payload["pair"][1]),
        },
    )


@web_app.get(_STATE_STRIP)
async def state_strip(request: Request, stem: str) -> Response:
    """Serve the state strip — the poll's swap target, the trigger re-armed.

    Purpose: consume state (the query — never refuses on coverage): the
    census read verbatim (total + the per-item involvement) at 200; the
    returned fragment carries the same every-5s trigger — the poll re-arms.
    404 (the unknown stem) => the refusal fragment at 200.
    Refuses when: never by this hand.
    Re-run: deterministic given the store state.
    Touches: nothing — a query.
    Provenance: web-brief §4 route 9, the design §8, G-WEBSPEC-BRIEF.
    """
    result = await _service("GET", f"/runs/{stem}/state")
    if result.status_code != _OK:
        return _refuse_fragment(request, _fields(result.json()))
    body = result.json()
    return templates.TemplateResponse(
        request,
        "state-strip.html",
        {"stem": stem, "total": int(body["total"]), "items": dict[str, int](body["items"])},
    )
```

```python
# Copyright (C) 2026 Mark Losey. All rights reserved.
"""web-scaffold the front end from the source structure — the only writer.

The web unit's GENERATOR (web-brief §1.2/§3d): a REGEN-TIME emitter, never a
runtime render — `uv run python scripts/generation/web_scaffold.py --target
web` writes the front end's artifacts from web_structure.py (the sibling
data module; the script-run's own path root carries the import — no
importlib machinery), every file regen-stamped with the two-line header in
its file type's comment form; `--check` regenerates IN MEMORY and diffs the
tree — a divergence is a REFUSAL naming the re-run (the never-hand-edit law
enforced, the zero-findings bar's sibling; the Makefile's web-check target
rides the same argv). The `--root` argv (default the working directory)
names the tree the artifacts live under — the --check divergence test runs
against a tmp copy, never mutating the tracked tree. THE EMISSION
DISCIPLINE: the @KEY@ sentinels substitute from the structure's PINS +
COPY (the copy values' {slot} placeholders convert to Jinja2 slots at
substitution — the mechanical brace doubling, applied ONLY to the values,
never to the template bodies' own {stem} literals which the generated JS
substitutes at browse time); @VERDICT_BUTTONS@ substitutes the verdict
button map as a JSON dict literal (a valid Jinja2 dict). Hand-authored
artifacts are out of grammar; this script is the only writer.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import web_structure

__all__ = ["main"]

# The regen idiom (the AGENTS.md:1-2 precedent, the structure named IN the
# header) — composed per file type's comment form at emission.
_GENERATED_NOTE: str = (
    "@generated by scripts/generation/web_scaffold.py "
    "from scripts/generation/web_structure.py — do not edit manually"
)
_REGEN_LINE: str = "regen: uv run python scripts/generation/web_scaffold.py --target web"


def _slots(value: str) -> str:
    """Convert a copy value's {slot} placeholders to Jinja2 slots.

    Purpose: the mechanical brace doubling applied ONLY to substitution
    values — {quorum} becomes {{ quorum }} (a slot name may carry a filter:
    {components | length} becomes {{ components | length }}); the template
    bodies' own {stem} literals (data-pt-path, the generated JS's runtime
    substitution) are NEVER passed through here.
    Refuses when: never — a pure string transform.
    Re-run: deterministic — the same value converts the same way.
    Touches: nothing.
    Provenance: web-brief §8.3 (the emission discipline), G-WEBSPEC-BRIEF.
    """
    return value.replace("{", "{{").replace("}", "}}")


def _expand(body: str) -> str:
    """Expand a template body's @KEY@ sentinels from the structure's data.

    Purpose: one substitution pass — PINS (the CDN URLs) + COPY (the copy
    values, slot-converted) + the VERDICT_BUTTONS map as a JSON dict
    literal; the structure is the emission's only source (R1: the entire
    front end generated from Python).
    Refuses when: never — unknown sentinels ride through untouched (an
    authoring error surfaces at the --check diff or the face tests, never
    silently).
    Re-run: deterministic — the same body expands to the same bytes.
    Touches: nothing — the in-memory expansion; the writer persists it.
    Provenance: web-brief §3d (the emission channel), G-WEBSPEC-BRIEF.
    """
    expanded = body
    for key, value in web_structure.PINS.items():
        expanded = expanded.replace(f"@{key}@", value)
    for key, value in web_structure.COPY.items():
        expanded = expanded.replace(f"@{key}@", _slots(value))
    return expanded.replace("@VERDICT_BUTTONS@", json.dumps(web_structure.VERDICT_BUTTONS))


def _headers(suffix: str) -> str:
    """Compose the two-line regen header in the file type's comment form.

    Purpose: every artifact carries the idiom — HTML the comment form, CSS
    the block-comment form, JS the line-comment form; the header names the
    generator, the structure, and the re-run command (the never-hand-edit
    law, readable at every artifact's head).
    Refuses when: an unknown suffix — ValueError (an emission form for an
    unmapped file type is an authoring error, loud at generation time).
    Re-run: deterministic.
    Touches: nothing.
    Provenance: web-brief §3d (the regen-stamp), the AGENTS.md:1-2 idiom.
    """
    if suffix == ".html":
        return f"<!-- {_GENERATED_NOTE} -->\n<!-- {_REGEN_LINE} -->\n"
    if suffix == ".css":
        return f"/* {_GENERATED_NOTE} */\n/* {_REGEN_LINE} */\n"
    if suffix == ".js":
        return f"// {_GENERATED_NOTE}\n// {_REGEN_LINE}\n"
    message = f"no regen header form for the suffix {suffix!r}"
    raise ValueError(message)


def _plan(root: Path) -> list[tuple[Path, str]]:
    """Plan the artifact set — every (path, bytes) the emission owns.

    Purpose: the ONE plan both writers share: the 14 templates under
    web/templates/ (the base + the eight screens + the five fragments, in
    the structure's inventory order) + web/static/app.css (the structure's
    stylesheet) + web/static/app.js (the structure's Web Components surface)
    — 16 artifacts, each the header + the expanded body, byte-determined by
    the structure alone.
    Refuses when: never — a pure projection.
    Re-run: deterministic — the same structure plans the same bytes.
    Touches: nothing — the caller writes or diffs.
    Provenance: web-brief §1.4 (the emission home), §3d, G-WEBSPEC-BRIEF.
    """
    artifacts: list[tuple[Path, str]] = []
    for name, body in web_structure.TEMPLATES.items():
        path = root / "web" / "templates" / name
        artifacts.append((path, _headers(path.suffix) + _expand(body)))
    artifacts.append((root / "web" / "static" / "app.css", _headers(".css") + web_structure.STYLESHEET))
    artifacts.append((root / "web" / "static" / "app.js", _headers(".js") + web_structure.APP_JS))
    return artifacts


def _emit(root: Path) -> None:
    """Write the artifact set — the front end's only writer at work.

    Purpose: create the homes (mkdir parents), write every artifact with
    UTF-8 encoding, print the count + the home (the tool's report channel —
    the T201 named ruling rides pyproject; the cli.py precedent re-carried).
    Refuses when: never — an unwritable root raises through the OS (loud).
    Re-run: idempotent — the same structure re-emits byte-identical bytes.
    Touches: the web/ tree under the root — the 16 artifacts, nothing else.
    Provenance: web-brief §3d (the emission channel), G-WEBSPEC-BRIEF.
    """
    artifacts = _plan(root)
    for path, content in artifacts:
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        path.write_text(content, encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"emitted {len(artifacts)} web artifacts under {root / 'web'}")


def _check(root: Path) -> int:
    """Diff the tree against the in-memory regeneration — the never-hand-edit law's enforcement.

    Purpose: regenerate every artifact in memory and compare with the
    disk's bytes; a divergence prints each divergent path + the re-run
    command and returns 1 (the refusal names the cure — a REFUSAL, never a
    silent diff); sync prints the all-clear and returns 0. The web-check
    make target and the --check test ride this one exit code.
    Refuses when: the tree diverges — that is the op's one refusal (a
    missing artifact is a divergence: None never equals the planned bytes).
    Re-run: deterministic — the same tree checks the same way.
    Touches: nothing — the check never writes (the tracked tree is never
    mutated by a check).
    Provenance: web-brief §3d (--check), §6.2, G-WEBSPEC-BRIEF.
    """
    divergences: list[str] = []
    for path, content in _plan(root):
        on_disk = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8") if path.exists() else None
        if on_disk != content:
            divergences.append(str(path))
    if divergences:
        for divergence in divergences:
            print(f"web artifacts diverge from the source structure: {divergence}")
        print(f"re-run: uv run python scripts/generation/web_scaffold.py --target web --root {root}")
        return 1
    print("web artifacts in sync with the source structure")
    return 0


def main() -> int:
    """Drive the scaffold — --target web writes; --check diffs.

    Purpose: the argparse surface: --target (the emission's target, "web"
    the only one — the ruling names the future widening), --check (the diff
    mode), --root (the tree under which web/ lives, the working directory
    by default — the repo-root launch discipline held; the divergence test
    passes a tmp root). Returns the process exit code (0 sync/emitted, 1
    divergence).
    Refuses when: --target anything but web — argparse's choices refusal
    (exit 2, the named-cure form).
    Re-run: deterministic — the same argv checks/emits the same way.
    Touches: the web/ tree under --root on the write path; nothing on --check.
    Provenance: web-brief §3d (the argv), §1.8 (web-check), G-WEBSPEC-BRIEF.
    """
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="web-scaffold the front end from the source structure")
    parser.add_argument("--target", choices=["web"], required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--check", action="store_true")
    parser.add_argument("--root", type=Path, default=Path("."))
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if args.check:
        return _check(args.root)
    _emit(args.root)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
```

```js
// app.js — the web tier's Web Components: pt-copy + the data-pt-path navigation delegation (web-brief §4 route 1; the design §5 — authored source per R9/R10)
class PtCopy extends HTMLElement {
  connectedCallback() {
    const value = this.getAttribute("value") ?? "";
    const label = this.getAttribute("label") ?? "Copy";
    const button = document.createElement("sl-button");
    button.textContent = label;
    button.addEventListener("click", () => {
      navigator.clipboard.writeText(value);
      button.textContent = "Copied";
      window.setTimeout(() => { button.textContent = label; }, 2000);
    });
    this.replaceChildren(button);
  }
}
customElements.define("pt-copy", PtCopy);
document.addEventListener("submit", (event) => {
  const form = event.target;
  const path = form.getAttribute("data-pt-path");
  if (path === null) { return; }
  event.preventDefault();
  const stem = form.querySelector("input[name='stem']").value.trim();
  if (stem) { window.location.assign(path.replace("{stem}", encodeURIComponent(stem))); }
});
```

```python
rendering fragments at 200); the in-process service client (httpx2
.AsyncClient over ASGITransport against the imported service app —
raise_app_exceptions=False REQUIRED: the service fold sends its envelope
then always re-raises, and the fold case needs the envelope RETURNED, rikai
finding 1 ruled); THE LOADER/RENDER SEAM (R10's three beats): the front
end's content lives in AUTHORED FILES — the Jinja2 templates under
web/templates/ (each file the source of truth for its surface, edited by
definition — the never-hand-edit law's scope never reaches them) and the
static assets under web/static/ (app.css + the Web Components app.js) —
and THIS module LOADS them (Jinja2Templates' filesystem loader + the
StaticFiles mount) and GENERATES the served surface from them at request
time (template + context -> the page); ZERO template content lives in
Python (no string constants, no giant concatenations — the superseded
web_structure.py form out of grammar), ZERO generated artifacts (nothing
emits, nothing regens, no --check). The CWD-relative homes ride the
repo-root launch discipline (STORE_HOME run_store.py:53 the precedent);
the static mount's check_dir=False is the named cure for the acceptance
harness's scratch-cwd boot (StaticFiles raises at import on an absent
directory; the store mkdirs on demand — the asymmetry named at the
re-settle). The child's OWN fold + refuse handlers (the mount's price:
after the tail mount every path the parent does not fully match lands on
the child — starlette routing.py serves the FIRST FULL match and the
Mount matches FULL on path alone, so the child owns the unmatched-path and
disallowed-method surface; its refuse handler renders the IDENTICAL family
grammar as a JSONResponse so the pinned parent-face arcs survive
unedited); the no-anchoring law held by construction (the count fields are
UNREAD at every sitting-context controller — they never enter a render
context); the fragment routes parse form bodies MANUALLY (no typed Form
fields: FastAPI's validation 422 would emit outside the family grammar,
and the fragment tier holds no 4xx — the wire is the sole validator). All
imports via fastapi/starlette's re-export surface + httpx2 (the lock's
name — NEVER `import httpx`, the stale unlocked venv copy; alias_httpx()
library-forbidden). Five-field docstrings on every public symbol;
content-in-configuration (the paths and template names named constants); no
asserts, no prints.
```
